 ORDER
This is the First application u/S.439 Cr.P.C filed by the applicant for grant of bail.
Applicant has been arrested on 28/09/2019 by Police Station- Thatipur, District-Gwalior (M.P.) in connection with Crime No.504/2019 for the offence punishable under Sections 302 and 34 of IPC.

According to prosecution case, on 28/09/2019, the complainant- Ku. Palak Shakya gave an information to police stating that on 28-09-2019 at the preceding night about 01:30 am, when she along with her mother Leela Shakya was sleeping in her house, they heard that some is knocking the gate whereby they woke up.
Her mother Leela Shakya went for open the gate and she also accompanied her mother.

As soon as the door was opened, the present applicant who is her uncle (Tau) Suneel Shakya along with Tillan Shakya, aunt (tai) Leela Devi Shakya started committing marpeet with her mother and they were loudly telling her that you have falsely implicated in 376 Vishal @ Tillan vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 20 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/38857789/

Her Tai Leela Devi caught hold of hands of her mother, present applicant Suneel Shakya by means of iron rod (Sariya) and Tillan by means of stick (Danda)
committed marpeet with her mother due to which blood started oozing out.
Due to scare, she climbed on the roof.
Thereafter, co- accused Tillan Shakya took her mother behind the house and after throwing stones killed her mother.
On the basis of such information, Crime No.504 of 2019 was registered for offence under Section 302, 34 of IPC against the present applicant and co-accused Tillan Shakya and Leela Devi Shakya.
Dead body panchnama was prepared and it was sent for postmortem and as per postmortem, the deceased died due to multiple injuries and cause of death was homicidal in nature.
The applicant along with other co-accused were arrested.
After completion of investigation, charge sheet was filed.
It is submitted by counsel for the applicant that applicant is aged 21 years and he has been falsely implicated in this case.
After investigation, charge-sheet has been submitted, therefore, further custodial interrogation is not required in the matter.
Out of 13 witnesses, seven witnesses including all material witnesses i.e. complainant have been examined.

It is further submitted that Co-accused- Suneel Shakya has already been released on bail by this Court vide order dated 03/05/2023 passed in MCRC No.2609/2023 and case of the applicant is similar to the said co-accused.
The applicant is in custody since 29/09/2019 and he is the permanent resident of District- Gwalior (M.P.).
There is no likelihood of his absconsion or tampering with the prosecution evidence.
Conclusion of trial will take some time.
Hence, prayed for grant of bail.
On the other hand, learned counsel for the State vehemently opposed the application and prayed for its rejection.
Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the case diary as well as charge sheet.

Looking to the aforesaid aforesaid facts & circumstances of the case as well as the facts that charge-sheet has been filed, all the material witnesses have been examined, the applicant is in custody since 28/09/2019 and conclusion of trial will take some time, without commenting upon merits of the case, this Court is of the opinion that the application should be allowed and by allowing the application it is ordered that if the applicant furnishes a cash surety of Rs.25,000/- alongwith a personal bail bond of Rs.25,000/- (Rupees twenty five thousand only) to the satisfaction of the trial Court, he should be released on bail.
He will present during trial before the trial Court on each and every date.
In case of any default, cash surety of Rs. 25,000/- shall stand forfeited automatically.

Accordingly, present application preferred under Section 439 of Cr.P.C.
by the applicant stands allowed and disposed of.
